name: GEORGIA

flag.title: Flag of Georgia
flag.note: White with red cross & four red crosses

lead: Georgia sits between the Caucasus mountains and the Black Sea. People made the first wine here 8,000 years ago. Georgian singers weave three voices together, and one song flew into space. Its alphabet is found nowhere else.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Founded c. 458 AD by hot springs

geo: Georgia lies where Europe meets Asia. Snowy mountains form a giant wall in the north. Mount Shkhara rises 5,201 m, taller than any Alpine peak.
The west is warm and wet from Black Sea breezes. The east is drier. Hot sulphur springs bubble up in the city of Tbilisi.
animals: The East Caucasian tur is a wild goat with curved horns. It climbs cliffs up to 4,000 m. The Caucasian leopard is the largest leopard subspecies.
Each autumn, over one million birds of prey fly past Batumi on the Black Sea coast. The Caucasian salamander lives in the western rainforests.
culture: Georgians have made wine for 8,000 years in qvevri, clay jars buried underground. The wine ferments slowly in cool earth. UNESCO listed this method in 2013.
Georgian polyphonic singing is one of the oldest kinds of music on Earth. UNESCO lists it too. The alphabet, mkhedruli, dates to the 5th century.
history: Western Georgia was once Colchis, where the Greek hero Jason sought the Golden Fleece. By the 11th century, a Georgian kingdom reached the Caspian Sea.
Russia took over in the 19th century, then the Soviet Union in 1921. Georgia declared independence on 9 April 1991, and it still guards its old identity.
wows: Grape traces 8,000 years old were found near Tbilisi.
The song Chakrulo rode into space on Voyager in 1977.
Legend says a king’s falcon dropped its prey into hot springs, and Tbilisi grew there.
Over one million birds of prey pass Batumi each autumn.
Georgia has over 500 local grape types.
Three old Georgian scripts are UNESCO heritage.

myths.myth: Georgia is named after Saint George
myths.fact: Many experts think the name comes from Gurj, a Persian word. Georgians call their land by a very different name.

myths.myth: Georgian cheese bread is just pizza
myths.fact: It is khachapuri. The boat-shaped kind holds a runny egg and butter. You tear the crust and dip it in.
